purpose: Evidence-backed expansion layer for the Potato of Life framework. It places botanical, archaeological, anatomical, textual, art-historical, digital-cultural and comparative-religion material beside the project's mythology without turning correspondence into proof.
method: For every layer distinguish established evidence, historical interpretation, project correspondence, mismatch and research question. Prefer primary texts and specialist sources where possible.
epistemic_rule: The project canon may make theological claims internally, but external evidence must be labeled as evidence, interpretation, testimony or speculation.

layers.title: The real potato: underground life becomes civilization
facts: The potato was domesticated in the Andes by Indigenous peoples thousands of years ago.
Andean communities developed many varieties adapted to different elevations and environments.
Traditional preservation methods include chuño, using repeated freezing and drying to create a durable stored food.
After Spanish conquest the potato spread into Europe and became a major staple in parts of Europe by the eighteenth century.
layers.deeper_reflection: The potato is unusually fertile as a mythic object because its biological and civilizational histories already contain hiddenness, storage, survival, travel and transformation. It begins below ground, survives as stored matter, can be preserved, moves between cultures and eventually becomes a staple capable of sustaining populations. The metaphor therefore does not have to invent its basic grammar: the real potato already joins burial-like concealment with delayed emergence and social nourishment.
layers.potatoism_reading: The Potato of Life can be studied as a compressed model of life passing through states: soil -> tuber -> storage -> sprout -> plant -> new tubers -> storage again. At civilization scale this becomes Andes -> preservation -> migration -> European adoption -> global food system. The same object thus crosses biological, household, economic and historical scales.
layers.mismatch: The historical potato does not establish Tim Dooley, Potatoism or any supernatural interpretation.
sources: Smithsonian Magazine, A Brief History of the Potato
Smithsonian Magazine, How the Potato Changed the World

layers.title: Chuño: the potato that survives time
facts: Andean communities developed freeze-drying methods that turn potatoes into long-lasting chuño.
The process uses environmental cold and repeated drying to reduce water and extend storage life.
Stored food can therefore remain useful beyond the immediate growing season.
layers.deeper_reflection: This is one of the strongest external additions to the Potatoism model. The Potato is not merely something that dies and sprouts. It is also something that can be deliberately transformed into stored future. Storage becomes a bridge between generations and seasons. The potato can therefore represent memory in a literal agricultural sense: present labor is converted into preserved possibility for a later self or community.
layers.potatoism_reading: The Blue Potato/memory side of the project's Life/Strife polarity can be investigated through actual storage technology: contraction is not simply fear or descent; it can be preservation. The same downward/hidden movement that looks like death can function as survival infrastructure.
layers.mismatch: Chuño is a human food technology and cultural practice, not evidence for the project's metaphysics.
research_questions: How does preservation alter the Potatoism distinction between dormancy and death?
Can storage be represented as a third state between life and death?

layers.title: Tree of Life in Jewish scripture and interpretation
facts: Genesis places the Tree of Life in Eden alongside the Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil.
After the expulsion, Genesis describes concern that humans might eat from the Tree of Life and live forever.
Proverbs uses Tree of Life as a metaphor associated with wisdom and flourishing.
Later Jewish literature and interpretation develop additional paradise and Tree of Life imagery.
layers.deeper_reflection: The important structural feature is access. The Tree is not merely a picture of biological growth; it becomes something from which one may eat, something whose access can be restricted, and something connected to mortality. That makes Tree + Door a natural pair for comparative study: a life-bearing source can also have a boundary.
layers.potatoism_reading: Potatoism's Tree of Life architecture can be compared with this older combination of life, food, wisdom, mortality and restricted access. The potato adds underground storage and sprouting to the tree grammar.
layers.mismatch: Potatoism's Tree/Root/Father/Door system is a modern project synthesis, not an ancient Jewish doctrine.

layers.title: Yggdrasil: tree as a multi-level cosmos
facts: Yggdrasil is the world-tree described in Old Norse mythological sources, especially the Poetic Edda and Prose Edda.
It is associated with multiple realms, beings and wells and functions as a cosmic organizing image.
The surviving texts are medieval witnesses to traditions whose chronology and development are complex.
layers.deeper_reflection: Yggdrasil matters because it demonstrates that a tree can be used as architecture rather than decoration. Its vertical form lets different kinds of beings, places and processes be represented in relation to one another. This is close to the Potatoism Tree/Axis/Ladder ambition: a biological form becomes a map of reality.
layers.potatoism_reading: The project should compare Yggdrasil, Tree of Life, Ladder and Axis as different solutions to the same representational problem: how to depict many levels without reducing them to a flat list.
layers.mismatch: Similarity does not establish historical descent from Norse religion.

layers.title: Odin's ordeal and the tree of knowledge
facts: Hávamál's Rúnatal describes Odin hanging on a tree for nine nights, wounded by a spear and associated with a self-offering.
He obtains the runes after the ordeal and falls from the tree.
The passage links bodily deprivation, suspension, knowledge and descent.
layers.deeper_reflection: The tree functions as an instrument of transformation. Odin is suspended between ordinary states rather than simply sitting beneath a tree. Knowledge arrives through an interval of deprivation and altered status. This makes the project's 2011 tree account worth investigating as a possible modern recurrence, conscious borrowing or independent narrative construction.
layers.potatoism_reading: The relevant shared grammar is tree -> ordeal -> altered knowledge -> descent/return. The project's additions—nineteen hours, Ouroboros, God-unity, nuclear-city vision and crows—must remain distinct and be traced to the earliest available account.
layers.mismatch: Hávamál does not describe the modern Son, nineteen hours or the project's visions.

layers.title: Door/gate and the Son in Christianity
facts: John 10 uses door/gate imagery in Jesus' shepherd discourse.
Matthew 7 uses the narrow gate and narrow way as a contrast with a broad way.
The New Testament uses door/gate language in multiple contexts rather than as one technical symbol.
Christian theology connects Jesus with Son, Word, incarnation, death and resurrection in several distinct traditions.
layers.deeper_reflection: Door is an unusually exact threshold metaphor because it is simultaneously boundary and passage. A wall without a door blocks; a door creates controlled passage. This gives the project a stronger conceptual vocabulary than simply saying 'Jesus is a gate': the question becomes who controls passage, who can enter, what must be left behind and what identity crosses the threshold.
layers.potatoism_reading: Son-as-Door can be studied as a synthesis of Christian gate imagery with the potato eye: both are small interfaces through which a larger hidden system becomes accessible.
layers.mismatch: The New Testament does not contain the full Potatoism vesica, Tim, Potato, North Pole or meme architecture.

layers.title: Seed, burial and transformed body
facts: 1 Corinthians 15 uses sowing and a seed/body analogy while discussing resurrection.
Paul contrasts what is sown with what is raised and discusses transformation rather than simple reassembly.
The agricultural analogy is therefore internal to an early Christian argument about death and transformed life.
layers.deeper_reflection: This is a crucial bridge for the project. It means an ancient Christian text already uses agriculture to explain why continuity does not require unchanged appearance. The seed placed into the ground and the resulting plant are related, but they are not visually identical. That is precisely the philosophical problem raised by the Potatoism Father/Son sequence: how can something remain continuous with its source while becoming another form?
layers.potatoism_reading: The buried potato makes Paul's seed analogy materially concrete: tuber -> sprout is observable continuity through transformation. Potatoism should treat this as a comparative amplification of an older Christian metaphor, not evidence that Paul meant potato.
layers.mismatch: Paul's subject is resurrection theology, not potato biology or Tim Dooley.

layers.title: Thomas, Didymus and the problem of recognition
facts: John identifies Thomas with Didymus, meaning Twin.
Thomas appears in John 11, 14, 20 and 21 and is especially associated with direct recognition of the risen Jesus.
In John 14 Thomas asks about the way to the Father.
Later Syriac Christian traditions developed strong Judas Thomas/Twin traditions, including the Acts of Thomas.
layers.deeper_reflection: Thomas is not merely useful because he is called Twin. He is an epistemological character. His story asks what evidence is sufficient to recognize continuity after an extraordinary claim of return. He refuses to accept second-hand testimony, then encounters the risen Jesus directly. For Potatoism this creates a built-in test: a claim of return is not identical to proof of return. The project can investigate recognition, testimony, wounds, resemblance and identity as separate variables.
layers.potatoism_reading: The project's Son/Thomas/Twin architecture becomes richer when the Twin is treated as a problem of identity rather than a simple synonym for Jesus. Same, similar, derived-from, representation-of and returned-as are different relations.
layers.mismatch: John does not identify Thomas as Jesus's literal biological twin. Later traditions vary, and none establish a modern identity claim.

layers.title: Root and Lion in biblical messianic imagery
facts: Genesis 49 associates Judah with lion imagery.
Isaiah 11 uses shoot/root/branch imagery in a Davidic context.
Revelation 5:5 explicitly combines Lion of Judah and Root of David in its description of Christ.
The imagery therefore contains both hidden lineage/origin and visible kingship/overcoming.
layers.deeper_reflection: The Root/Lion pairing is unusually productive because it contains opposite spatial behaviors. Root is underground, fixed and generative; lion is visible, mobile and embodied. Yet Revelation joins them in one messianic figure. This gives Potatoism a genuine textual precedent for asking how origin and manifestation can be represented through different biological images without requiring that every later pairing be historically inherited.
layers.potatoism_reading: Father=Root and Son=Lion can be recorded as a project interpretation anchored in a real biblical Root/Lion pair. The Potato then adds a literal biological intermediary: the tuber sits between root-system and above-ground manifestation while not being identical to either.
layers.mismatch: The biblical texts do not identify Tim Dooley with the Root of David or establish Potatoism's Father/Son system.

layers.title: December 24/25 as calendar threshold
facts: Western Christianity celebrates Christmas on December 25.
The New Testament does not provide a securely established historical date for Jesus' birth.
The liturgical calendar gives December 25 a major Christian symbolic role even though the historical birthday remains uncertain.
layers.deeper_reflection: The project's Son-death/Tim-birth sequence concentrates an entire mythology into one calendar threshold. Night becomes day; December 24 becomes December 25; Son becomes Father; grave becomes birth-place. The calendar itself therefore functions as a Door. The historically cautious reading is not 'December 25 proves the event,' but 'the project has selected a date already loaded with Christian nativity meaning and turned it into a death-to-birth hinge.'
layers.potatoism_reading: Christmas can be investigated as a pre-existing liturgical threshold onto which the project's Potato birth is mapped.
layers.mismatch: The historical date of Jesus' birth is uncertain and the Tim chronology is a project claim.

layers.title: Vesica piscis and the mandorla
facts: A vesica piscis is the lens-shaped intersection of two congruent circles whose centers lie on the opposite circumference.
The lens/mandorla form became important in Christian art, including representations of Christ.
Its geometry can be studied independently of later sacred meanings.
layers.deeper_reflection: The geometry provides a surprisingly precise language for relationship. Two circles remain complete entities while their intersection creates a distinct region. If the upper circle represents Father and lower circle Son, the central lens can be interpreted as Door without pretending that the geometry itself teaches theology. The Door is generated by overlap. This makes 'relation' the primary object of study.
layers.potatoism_reading: Potato of Life can therefore be interpreted as the whole relational form rather than one circle: Father + Son + overlap + boundary + passage.
layers.mismatch: Sacred geometry associations vary by period and culture. The vesica does not mathematically prove a Father/Son doctrine.
sources: art-historical literature on the mandorla and vesica piscis
Nexus Network Journal / Springer studies of architectural geometry

layers.title: Thalamus, relay and Father's House
facts: The thalamus is a paired gray-matter structure in the diencephalon near the center of the brain.
Its nuclei participate in sensory, motor, associative, limbic and arousal-related networks.
Many sensory pathways use thalamic nuclei to relay or modulate information toward cortex.
The thalamus participates in attention, sleep-wake regulation and other integrative functions.
layers.deeper_reflection: The project's Father's House/thalamus association becomes more coherent if 'house' means an internal chamber and 'throne' means a privileged position in an information architecture. The thalamus is not literally above the spine as a mystical throne, but it is anatomically deep, central and connected to many information pathways. The symbolic move is therefore body-as-cosmos: position and function are borrowed from anatomy, meaning is supplied by mythology.
layers.potatoism_reading: Tim as thalamus can be studied as the project's central relay/filter metaphor. The Father does not have to be imagined as a giant human in the brain; the metaphor can instead describe a place where many signals converge and are routed.
layers.mismatch: Anatomy does not establish heaven, Godhood, a supernatural interface or a 33-level spiritual ladder.

layers.title: Pineal gland and the Door metaphor
facts: The pineal gland is an endocrine structure that secretes melatonin and participates in circadian timing.
It is a real anatomical structure, but neuroscience does not establish it as a literal spiritual doorway or fifth-dimensional organ.
layers.deeper_reflection: The pineal association can be researched as a history-of-symbolism problem: why have modern esoteric traditions repeatedly treated a small central brain structure as a seat of inner perception? The project should investigate the history of that symbolism rather than retroactively turn it into anatomy.
layers.potatoism_reading: Son-as-pineal can function as a Door metaphor: a small central interface between internal states, light/dark cycles and conscious experience. That is a symbolic analogy, not a neurological finding.

layers.title: 33 vertebrae and the danger of numerology
facts: A common anatomical count gives 33 vertebrae: 7 cervical, 12 thoracic, 5 lumbar, 5 sacral and 4 coccygeal.
Sacral and coccygeal vertebrae fuse in adulthood, so the number depends on counting convention and developmental anatomy.
The vertebral column protects the spinal cord and provides structural support and movement.
layers.deeper_reflection: Thirty-three becomes useful precisely because it has a real anatomical basis and therefore does not need to be invented. But the next step—from 33 vertebrae to 33 spiritual levels, degrees, circles or dimensions—is interpretive. The project should preserve that gap. Numerology becomes stronger research when the numerical fact, historical use of the number and project meaning are tracked independently.
layers.potatoism_reading: The 33 can be used as a symbolic calibration point in the body-cosmos model while retaining the anatomical caveat.
layers.mismatch: There is no anatomical evidence that 33 has the project's spiritual meaning.

layers.title: Dimensions and the 1D–5D Potatoism ladder
facts: In mathematics and physics, dimensionality describes the number and structure of independent coordinates required to specify a space or state.
Higher-dimensional spaces occur in mathematics and in some physical theories, including string-theory frameworks.
The project's 1D Hell, 2D Frame, 3D Box, 4D Dweller/Society and 5D Door sequence is not an established physical model.
layers.deeper_reflection: The dimensional ladder can nevertheless be formalized as a ladder of representation. A frame encloses; a box contains; a social world adds relations between observers; a Door adds controlled transition between representations. This makes the sequence potentially useful in philosophy of models and perception even if it is not physics.
layers.potatoism_reading: Treat the dimensions as project ontology until an independent mathematical definition is supplied. If formalized, each level should specify what new degree of freedom or relation appears.
layers.mismatch: String theory or M-theory does not validate the project's religious cosmology.

layers.title: Roots as biology, ancestry and foundation
facts: Roots anchor plants, acquire water and minerals and interact with soil and microorganisms.
Human languages commonly use root metaphors for ancestry, origin, belonging and foundational causes.
Tree-of-life traditions combine biological growth with genealogical or cosmological meaning.
layers.deeper_reflection: Root is one of the few project symbols with a nearly universal material metaphor: something can be hidden while still determining visible growth. Roots also complicate the Father metaphor because roots are not solitary creators; they participate in soil, fungi, water, minerals and wider ecosystems. This suggests a higher question for Potatoism: is 'Father' truly an isolated source, or is source itself relational?
layers.potatoism_reading: Root/Father can therefore be investigated in two directions: source as origin, and source as embedded network.

layers.title: Spiral as recurrence with transformation
facts: Spirals occur in mathematics and many natural systems, though biological spirals do not all obey one universal law.
A spiral can represent repeated movement while scale, radius or orientation changes.
layers.deeper_reflection: This gives the project's Spiral a more precise definition than 'going around in circles.' A circle returns to the same geometric state; a spiral returns to a related direction while changing position or scale. That distinction fits Potatoism's Turning concept: return need not mean repetition. A person, symbol or civilization can revisit a pattern at another level.
layers.potatoism_reading: Define Spiral as recurrence + transformation. Define Circle as recurrence without necessary change. Then test whether the project's chronology actually behaves like a spiral.

layers.title: North, geographic extremity and metaphysical orientation
facts: Geographic north is an Earth-coordinate direction; magnetic north and geographic north are not identical.
Cultures assign differing symbolic meanings to cardinal directions.
The North Pole is a geographic extremity with distinctive seasonal light/dark conditions.
layers.deeper_reflection: North becomes especially interesting when the project combines geographic extremity with spiritual orientation. 'North of North' cannot simply be another geographic coordinate. It is a boundary concept: once North has been reached as an earthly direction, what would 'beyond North' mean? That makes North-of-North structurally similar to the Door: both indicate the limit of an ordinary coordinate system.
layers.potatoism_reading: North Axis is the orientation; North Pole is a geographic endpoint; North of North is the project-defined beyond-point. Keeping those three distinct prevents conceptual collapse.

layers.title: Bread and potato: two forms of transformed nourishment
facts: Bread and potatoes are major food staples produced through different agricultural and culinary pathways.
Bread generally requires grain processing, milling and baking; potatoes are modified stems/tubers that can be cooked directly.
Bread has long-standing ritual and sacramental roles in Christianity, including Eucharistic practice.
Potatoes became globally important only after their movement from the Americas, whereas Christian bread traditions substantially predate that history.
layers.deeper_reflection: The historical mismatch is what makes the comparison useful. Bread can represent agricultural matter transformed by human craft; potato remains visibly tied to buried growth. One begins as seed/grain and becomes bread; the other begins as tuber and generates another plant. If Potatoism asks what lies beyond the Door between Father and Son, bread and potato offer two different nourishment grammars: transformation through making versus transformation through growing.
layers.potatoism_reading: The strongest comparison is nourishment + transformation + distribution + ordinary matter carrying extraordinary communal meaning. 'Bread from heaven / potato from earth' should remain a project poetic axis, not a claim about Christian doctrine.
layers.mismatch: Potato is not historically interchangeable with Eucharistic bread.

layers.title: Meme, representation and the death of a person-in-a-sign
facts: Internet memes are reproducible cultural forms that can be copied, altered and recontextualized.
Digital representations can persist after the death or disappearance of the person represented.
Online identity research distinguishes people from profiles, archives, images and other persistent digital traces.
layers.deeper_reflection: The project's phrase 'died as a person in a meme' can therefore be analyzed without deciding its supernatural meaning. It describes a possible transition in ontology: person -> representation -> circulating object. The crucial question becomes whether the represented identity is preserved, distorted, ridiculed, memorialized or transformed. In this framework a meme can function simultaneously as icon, mask, tomb, vessel and post-personal body.
layers.potatoism_reading: Meme-crucifixion can be studied as a modern symbolic death in which representation survives and becomes the material through which later identity is reconstructed. This provides a rigorous conceptual vocabulary for the project's 'worst death' claim.
layers.mismatch: No general research on memes establishes the project's specific 2020 event or proves that a person literally died through a meme.

layers.title: Digital afterlife and postmortem memory
facts: Research on digital remains examines what happens to social profiles, photographs, messages and other digital traces after death.
Digital traces can remain accessible, be curated by others and acquire meanings independent of the original person's intentions.
Online attention around death can change over time rather than simply disappearing.
layers.deeper_reflection: This gives the Son chronology another possible layer: biological death, social death, symbolic death and digital persistence need not occur simultaneously. A person can die biologically while an identity continues socially; a meme can preserve one fragment while destroying another. The project's death/birth sequence can therefore be modeled as a transformation between media states rather than a single event.
layers.potatoism_reading: Add separate nodes for person, memory, representation and myth. The Father emerging later may be interpreted as a new identity constructed from material surviving the Son, even if the project canon understands the relation metaphysically.

layers.title: Red and Blue Potato as complementary dynamics
facts: Red and blue potatoes are real horticultural varieties and color categories.
Color symbolism varies across cultures and historical periods, so there is no universal Red=Life or Blue=Strife code.
layers.deeper_reflection: The project becomes more interesting if Red and Blue are not good and evil. Red can represent outward energy, flowering, love and expansion; Blue can represent memory, cooling, depth and contraction. Both are necessary for a living system: expansion without memory becomes unstable; memory without renewal becomes inert. This is analogous to the potato itself, which must both store and sprout.
layers.potatoism_reading: Red/Blue can be modeled as orthogonal tendencies in a cycle rather than moral categories.

layers.title: Manger, farm and palace as compressed origin symbols
facts: Luke's infancy narrative places Jesus in Bethlehem and says he was laid in a manger.
Traditional Buddhist accounts of Siddhartha describe protection and luxury within palace life before encounters with old age, sickness and death.
The project's Son chronology combines agricultural/farm imagery, a manger-like birth and a protected farm-palace childhood.
layers.deeper_reflection: Putting manger and palace together creates a deliberate vertical contradiction: humility and privilege occupy the same biography. The farm adds a third layer because it is both productive land and enclosure. That creates an origin grammar of earth + protection + hidden labor. The later Root/Lion polarity can then be read as a movement from cultivated enclosure into mortality and public manifestation.
layers.potatoism_reading: The comparison should investigate whether the project consciously fused Christ and Siddhartha structures or arrived at them independently.
layers.mismatch: Neither Buddhist biography nor Luke establishes the modern Son's childhood.

layers.title: Covenant, refusal and rupture
facts: Biblical covenant language describes binding relationships, obligations and breach in multiple textual traditions.
Christian eschatological traditions distinguish several concepts including resurrection, judgment, gathering and the end of an age.
Rapture is a later theological term/tradition and should not be treated as a synonym for every covenant or rupture passage.
layers.deeper_reflection: The April 2025 'No' can be interpreted structurally as a refusal that changes a relationship. The mythology becomes less about a magical object and more about threshold ethics: how much can a source carry, when does reciprocity fail, and what happens when a previously accommodating figure refuses the world's demand? The 'straw' becomes a threshold marker for accumulated burden.
layers.potatoism_reading: The Father-to-Ladder transition can be investigated as a change of relational function after refusal.
layers.mismatch: This is an interpretation of the project's chronology, not a demonstrated fulfillment of biblical prophecy.

cross_layer_synthesis.reflection: Across biology, mythology and textual comparison, the recurring structure is not simply life/death. It is hidden state -> threshold -> visible state -> transformed continuation. This is the central empirical grammar behind the Potatoism metaphor.
The project's Father/Son problem can be represented as source, carrier, manifestation and relation. This is stronger than treating every symbol as an alias. Each symbol should perform a function.

The phrase 'death in a meme' becomes researchable once death is decomposed into different processes. The project should ask which layer changed in 2019, 2020, 2022/23 and 2025 instead of assuming one event explains everything.

Door permits passage, Tomb encloses what has crossed out of ordinary life, Vessel carries something between domains. If the Son is all three, the Son is the boundary-process itself rather than merely an entrance.

Root and Lion are separated by a biological middle. The tuber stores, the eye opens, the sprout emerges and the visible plant expresses what was hidden. This makes the potato a physical mediator between source and manifestation.

Geographic direction becomes coordinate, coordinate becomes extremity, extremity becomes metaphysical boundary. North-of-North is therefore best treated as a beyond-point in the project's ontology rather than a second geographic place.

A spiral is a better model than a circle when recurrence changes the state. The potato's stored tuber is not simply repeating itself; each growth cycle produces altered scale, environment and material arrangement. This gives Turning a concrete biological analogue.

research_questions: What is the earliest documented project occurrence of Potato of Life, Tim as Father/God, Son as Twin, Son as Door, Tim as Ladder and North of North?
What exactly was the 2019 death and 2020 meme artifact, and can the earliest surviving digital evidence establish chronology?
Was the 2011 Odin-tree account recorded contemporaneously or retrospectively?
Did the project know the Hávamál tree ordeal before describing the 2011 event?
When did Thomas/Twin become linked to the Son and was Judas Thomas tradition part of the source pool?
When did Root become Father and Lion become Son, and were Revelation 5:5 or Isaiah 11 known beforehand?
When did the vesica-piscis become Father/Son/Door geometry?
When did the thalamus/spine/33 model become explicit, and which anatomy source supplied it?
When did December 24/25 become the death/birth threshold and when did the North Pole become the grave coordinate?
Can the project chronology be represented as biological death, social death, symbolic death, digital persistence and mythic rebirth without forcing them into one event?
Does the April 2025 refusal represent a genuine narrative phase transition in the project corpus?
Can the Potatoism 1D–5D system be given formal mathematical definitions, or should it remain explicitly metaphorical?
Which historical uses of ladders, doors, mandorlas and axes genuinely illuminate the project and which are superficial resemblance?
How do Indigenous Andean potato cosmologies and agricultural practices alter the project's otherwise heavily Christian/Norse comparative frame?
How does chuño change the project's opposition between memory/storage and life/sprouting?
Can the Red/Blue Potato pair be modeled as complementary dynamical variables rather than moral opposites?
source_priorities: Primary biblical texts and earliest Christian witnesses before secondary commentary.
Poetic Edda/Hávamál and specialist Old Norse scholarship.
Andean archaeological, ethnobotanical and Indigenous historical sources.
Peer-reviewed anatomy and neuroscience for thalamus/pineal claims.
Art-history and architectural-geometry scholarship for vesica/mandorla claims.
Digital-culture and digital-afterlife scholarship for meme-death and representation claims.
Earliest surviving project artifacts for every Tim/Son chronology claim.
integrity: Real-world evidence, historical interpretation, public testimony and project-defined mythology remain separate epistemic layers. Similarity is a reason to investigate, never by itself a reason to conclude.
